uncited: This family of methods modifies the fundamental 3D Gaussian primitive representation or the rendering kernel function used in 3D Gaussian Splatting to address specific limitations in shape modeling, surface reconstruction, and blur handling.

Unlike sibling methods that focus on training dynamics (e.g., [Densification Strategy](6234-densification-strategy.md)) or physical parameters ([Physical Parameter Optimization](4111-physical-parameter-optimization.md)), these techniques alter the mathematical definition of the splat itself—allowing negative colors, anchoring Gaussians to a grid, enforcing tangent-plane densification, replacing the Gaussian kernel with Radial Basis Functions, or modeling spatially-varying blur.

The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation defines a primitive $i$ by its position $\mathbf{p}_i$, covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_i$ (parameterized by rotation $\mathbf{R}_i$ and scale $\mathbf{s}_i$), opacity $\alpha_i$, and color $\mathbf{c}_i$ (often represented via spherical harmonics).
All methods in this family retain the differentiable rendering framework of 3D Gaussian Splatting [Parent].
The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting representation [Parent] assumes symmetric, positive-definite Gaussians with positive opacity and color.
Subsequent research identified limitations in modeling thin structures, complex shadows, and surface continuity.
